newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS strike over, flights normal again.
newsitem.headline: SAS strike over, flights normal again.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) SAS.OL said on Thursday that services were resuming as scheduled after ground staff ended a protest strike which had delayed some flights out of Copenhagen.

"Flights are getting back to normal after today's action, which involved 242 staff and started this morning. Over half our flights took off on time during the action and the bulk of the others only suffered delays of a maximum 25 minutes," SAS spokesman Jens Peter Skaarup told Reuters.
The strike involved check-in, ticket sales and other ancilliary workers, who had staged stoppages since Monday.
It ended after a union official formally apologised for entering a training class without authorisation and SAS management withdrew the reprimand against him which sparked the stoppage.
SAS suffered repeated waves of strikes throughout Scandinavia last year.
